title: Houses, flats and rooms
about: Collocations for finding and describing a home: the language of flat ads (short-let accommodation, fully furnished, off-road parking), describing rooms and buildings (a spacious living room, a draughty hall, a dilapidated building), and expressions with home like feel homesick and make yourself at home.

items.pattern: short-let accommodation / flats · a short let · noun + noun · accommodation is uncountable (UK)
items.meaning: a flat or room you can rent for a short time, from a few weeks to a few months
items.example: While our kitchen was being rebuilt, we stayed in **short-let accommodation** round the corner.
more: The company found him **short-let accommodation** for his three months in Leeds.
**Short-let flats** near the beach are booked up all summer.
items.watchOut: Accommodation у британській англійській зазвичай незлічуване: some accommodation, не an accommodation і не accommodations (accommodations частіше кажуть американці). Пишеться з двома c і двома m. Let тут — «здача в оренду»: a short let — короткострокова оренда.

items.pattern: a studio flat · a studio · US a studio apartment · noun + noun
items.meaning: a small flat for one person, where the living room, bedroom and kitchen are all one room
items.example: My first home was a **studio flat** above a bakery, and it always smelt of fresh bread.
more: A **studio flat** is perfect for one person, but it's too small for a couple with a dog.
In a **studio**, your bed is never far from the kitchen.
items.watchOut: Британці рахують спальні, а не кімнати: a two-bedroom flat — дві спальні плюс вітальня, тобто по-нашому радше трикімнатна квартира. Якщо житлова кімната, спальня й кухня — одне приміщення, це studio flat. Не плутай зі study — це кабінет.

items.pattern: move into a flat / house / new home · move in (no object) · ↔ move out of
items.meaning: start living in a new home
items.uk: в'їхати, переїхати (в нову квартиру чи будинок)
items.example: We **moved into** our new flat in March and still haven't hung any pictures.
more: My grandparents **moved into** this house in 1975 and never left.
The flat's empty now. The new tenants **move in** on Monday.
items.watchOut: «Переїхати в нову квартиру» — move into a new flat (можна й move to a new flat), але не move in a new flat. Без додатка — просто move in: When are you moving in? Enter — «увійти», а не «вселитися»: нові сусіди have moved into the house, а не entered into it.

items.pattern: suitable accommodation · suitable for sb/sth · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a place to live that is right for a particular person and their needs
items.example: It took us months to find **suitable accommodation** for a family with three dogs.
more: The council has to provide **suitable accommodation** for people who lose their homes.
The flat is lovely, but it isn't **suitable for** small children: the stairs are very steep.
items.watchOut: «Підходить для когось/чогось» — suitable for (suitable for children). Suitable to трапляється лише у формальній мові (suitable to their needs), а suitable with — помилка. Suitable — підходить саме тобі, твоїм потребам; comfortable — просто зручний.

items.pattern: a fully furnished flat / house · furnished ↔ unfurnished · adverb + adjective
items.meaning: with all the furniture you need already in it
items.example: The flat is **fully furnished**, so all you need to bring is your clothes.
more: **Unfurnished** flats are usually cheaper, but you have to buy a bed and a sofa.
We rented a **fully furnished** cottage, right down to the teaspoons.
items.watchOut: Furnished — «з меблями» (furniture), а не «з фурнітурою». «Повністю мебльований» — fully furnished; full furnished чи totally furnished так зазвичай не кажуть. Furniture незлічуване: a lot of furniture, a piece of furniture, не furnitures.

items.pattern: be available to rent (from…) · available for rent · UK signs: To let · adjective + to-infinitive
items.meaning: can be rented now or from a certain date
items.example: Two rooms above the café are **available to rent** from the end of the summer.
more: There's a 'To let' sign outside. Do you think the flat's **available to rent**?
Very few houses are **available to rent** in the village, so most young people move to town.
items.watchOut: Про житло, яке можна зняти, кажуть available, а не accessible: accessible — до якого легко дістатися (зокрема на візку). Табличка To let — «Здається»; for rent частіше пишуть американці. Житло британці rent (а власник його lets), а машину чи костюм частіше hire.

items.pattern: a (quiet) residential area / street / district · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a part of a town with houses and flats rather than offices, shops or factories
items.example: We live in a quiet **residential area**, but the shops are only ten minutes' walk away.
more: Cars have to go slowly in **residential streets** where children play.
The school is in a **residential area**, so the roads around it are quiet.
items.watchOut: «Житловий (спальний) район» — a residential area, не a living area (це зона відпочинку в квартирі) і не a sleeping district. Наголос на третій склад: resiDENtial.

items.pattern: £… per calendar month · pcm (in ads) · per week (pw)
items.meaning: for each month; used for rent in British property ads
items.example: The rent is £950 **per calendar month**, plus bills.
more: The ad said '£700 pcm', which means £700 **per calendar month**.
Is that price **per calendar month** or per week?
items.watchOut: Calendar month — місяць за календарем (наприклад, з 5 березня до 5 квітня). У розмові простіше: £950 a month або per month. Не «£950 in month» і не «for month». В оголошеннях скорочують: pcm — per calendar month, pw — per week.

items.pattern: a newly-built apartment / house / estate · the house is newly built · a new-build (UK, noun) · adverb + past participle
items.meaning: built only recently, so nobody has lived in it before
items.example: Our **newly-built** apartment still smells of fresh paint.
more: The **newly-built** houses by the river sold in a week.
We'd rather buy an old house than a **newly-built** one: the rooms are bigger.
items.watchOut: «Новобудова» — a new-build (UK) або a newly-built flat / house; a new building — просто «нова будівля». Newly — прислівник: newly-built, newly-painted, newly-married. Після дієслова зазвичай без дефіса: the house is newly built. Apartment у британських оголошеннях звучить трохи престижніше за flat.

items.pattern: a fully-fitted kitchen · fitted cupboards / wardrobes · adverb + past participle + noun
items.meaning: a kitchen that already has a cooker, cupboards and other equipment built in
items.uk: повністю обладнана кухня (з вбудованими меблями й технікою)
items.example: The flat has a **fully-fitted kitchen**: oven, dishwasher, the lot.
more: We spent most of our savings on a **fully-fitted kitchen** with an island in the middle.
**Fitted wardrobes** take up less space than free-standing ones.
items.watchOut: Fitted тут — «вбудований, зроблений під розмір». «Кухонний гарнітур» — a fitted kitchen або kitchen units, а не a kitchen set. Fully-equipped kitchen теж кажуть, але там акцент на техніці й посуді.

items.pattern: off-road parking · also off-street parking · a parking space · a car park
items.meaning: a place to leave your car that isn't on the street, such as a drive or a private car park
items.uk: місце для машини не на вулиці (власне паркомісце)
items.example: The house has **off-road parking** for two cars, which is rare in this part of town.
more: Without **off-road parking**, we spend ages looking for a space on the street every evening.
The new flats come with **off-road parking** at the back.
items.watchOut: Parking незлічуване: не a parking. «Паркінг» як місце — a car park (UK) або a parking lot (US), «паркомісце» — a parking space. A park — це парк. Off-road parking — місце для машини не на вулиці: під'їзна доріжка (a drive), двір, власний майданчик.

items.pattern: your / our dream home · a dream house / job / holiday · noun + noun
items.meaning: the perfect home that you have always wanted
items.example: After twenty years of saving, they've finally bought their **dream home** by the sea.
more: My **dream home** would have a big kitchen and a garden full of fruit trees.
The cottage needed a lot of work, but to us it was our **dream home**.
items.watchOut: «Дім моєї мрії» — my dream home: dream стоїть перед іменником як означення. Можна й the house of my dreams (у множині), а от my dreamed home так не кажуть. Так само: my dream job, a dream holiday.

items.pattern: a four-storey / two-storey / ten-storey house / building · storey (UK), story (US) · number + storey + noun
items.meaning: a house with four levels (floors), counting the ground floor
items.example: Our flat is in a **four-storey** house, and we've got the top floor.
more: Most houses in our street are **two-storey**, with a small garden at the back.
The new hospital is a **ten-storey** building, so you can see it from all over town.
items.watchOut: Про висоту будинку — storey: a four-storey house (без -s, бо це означення). Про те, на якому поверсі квартира, — floor: on the fourth floor. Американське написання — story. І пам'ятай: британський ground floor — наш перший поверх, first floor — наш другий.

items.pattern: a spacious living room / kitchen / flat · spacious accommodation · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a living room that is big and has a lot of space inside
items.example: The house has a **spacious living room** with a big fireplace and three windows.
more: The new flat feels **spacious** because there are hardly any walls.
The hotel rooms were **spacious** enough for a family of five.
items.watchOut: «Просторий» — spacious, не spatial: spatial — «просторовий», науковий термін (spatial awareness). Розмовний синонім — roomy.

items.pattern: have a (wonderful / great) view of sth · a room with a view · verb + noun + of
items.meaning: you can see something from a window or a place
items.uk: з вікон видно (щось); звідти відкривається вид на (щось)
items.example: Our kitchen **has a lovely view of** the hills.
more: Ask for a room on the top floor: they **have a view of** the cathedral.
We paid extra for a balcony with a **view of** the lake.
items.watchOut: «Вид на море» — a view of the sea (або a view over the sea), не a view on the sea: view on — це думка про щось (my view on this). «З вікна видно парк» — the window has a view of the park, а не the window sees the park.

items.pattern: a cosy study / room / flat / corner · a study = a room for working at home · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a small, warm, comfortable room where you work or read at home
items.example: Dad spends his evenings in his **cosy study** with a book and a cup of cocoa.
more: Our living room is **cosy** in winter, with thick curtains and a warm rug.
Mum has a little **study** under the stairs where she does the family's paperwork.
items.watchOut: Кабінет удома — a study, не cabinet: cabinet — шафка з дверцятами або уряд (the Cabinet). Cosy — британське написання, американське — cozy.

items.pattern: a light, airy room / bedroom / flat · light and airy · adjective + adjective + noun
items.meaning: full of daylight and fresh air, and feeling open
items.uk: світлі й просторі кімнати, де багато повітря
items.example: We loved the flat as soon as we saw its **light, airy** rooms.
more: I like **light, airy** rooms with white walls and not much furniture.
The café is **light and airy**, so it's a nice place to read in the morning.
items.watchOut: Light тут — «світлий, повний денного світла», а не «легкий». Airy — просторий і свіжий, з відчуттям повітря. Windy про кімнату не кажуть: windy — вітряний (про погоду, місце надворі).

items.pattern: a room / window / flat overlooks the garden / park / sea · verb + noun, no preposition
items.meaning: has a view of something, usually from above
items.example: The kitchen **overlooks** the garden, so I can keep an eye on the kids while I cook.
more: The hotel **overlooks** the harbour, so you can watch the boats over breakfast.
Their balcony **overlooks** a busy square, which is fun but noisy.
items.watchOut: «Вікна виходять на сад» — the windows overlook the garden, без прийменника: не overlook on / to. Можна й look onto / look out on the garden. Не плутай: overlook ще означає «не помітити, пропустити»: I overlooked a mistake.

items.pattern: a basement flat / kitchen · in the basement · noun + noun
items.meaning: a flat on the floor below street level
items.example: Our **basement flat** is cool in summer but a bit dark in winter.
more: You go down six steps from the street to reach the **basement flat**.
They keep their bikes in the **basement**.
items.watchOut: Basement — поверх нижче рівня вулиці, де живуть чи працюють; cellar — підвал-комора (для вина, вугілля, закруток). Квартира там — зазвичай a basement flat.

items.pattern: a granny flat · turn / convert sth into a granny flat · noun + noun, informal
items.meaning: a small separate flat in or next to a family house, where an older relative can live
items.uk: окрема квартирка при будинку для літніх родичів
items.example: My parents built a **granny flat** at the bottom of the garden, so Grandma lives close but has her own front door.
more: The **granny flat** is empty now, so we sometimes rent it to students.
Mum and Dad moved into the **granny flat** and gave the big house to us.
items.watchOut: Granny flat — розмовна назва житла, а не про саму бабусю: там може жити будь-хто. «Переробити гараж на квартиру» — turn / convert the garage into a flat, з прийменником into; remake і redo так не вживають.

items.pattern: add / build an extension (to / onto a house) · have an extension built · verb + noun
items.meaning: make your house bigger by building an extra room or rooms onto it
items.example: When the twins arrived, we **added an extension** with two more bedrooms.
more: Our neighbours are **building an extension**, so there's been drilling all week.
A glass **extension** turned their small kitchen into a sunny dining room.
items.watchOut: «Прибудова» — an extension, не expansion (розширення бізнесу, міста) і не extra building. Дієслово — add або build (розмовне put on an extension); make an extension так зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: be completely / fully refurbished · refurbish a flat / hotel / kitchen · a refurbishment · adverb + past participle
items.meaning: repaired, repainted and modernised so that it looks new
items.example: The hotel has been **completely refurbished**, and the rooms look brand new.
more: The flat was **completely refurbished** last year: new floors, new kitchen, new bathroom.
The library is closed while it's being **refurbished**.
items.watchOut: «Зробити ремонт» — refurbish, renovate або do up, а не make a repair чи make a remont. Repair — лагодити щось зламане: repair a roof, a tap. Refurbished — оновлений повністю: підлоги, фарба, кухня.

items.pattern: do up a house / flat / room · do sth up · phrasal verb, informal (UK)
items.meaning: make an old house or room look good again by fixing, painting and decorating it
items.example: We spent last summer **doing up** the old farmhouse, room by room.
more: They **did up** the spare room for the baby: new carpet, yellow walls and a little shelf for books.
It took them a year to **do the place up**, but now it looks amazing.
items.watchOut: Do up — розмовний відповідник refurbish. Частка тут — up: do in — розмовне «прикінчити», do down — «принижувати». З займенником вона стоїть після нього: do it up, не do up it.

items.pattern: move out of a flat / house · move out (no object) · ↔ move into
items.meaning: leave the place where you live and go to live somewhere else
items.example: Students have to **move out of** the halls of residence at the end of June.
more: We're **moving out** on Friday, so the whole flat is full of boxes.
When my brother **moved out**, I finally got the bedroom with the balcony.
items.watchOut: «Виїхати з квартири» — move out of the flat, не move off the flat. Move from — коли кажеш, звідки й куди: we moved from a flat to a house. Без додатка — просто move out: She moved out last year.

items.pattern: a dilapidated building / house / barn · adjective + noun
items.meaning: old and in very bad condition, falling to pieces
items.example: The cheapest flats are in a **dilapidated building** with broken windows and a leaking roof.
more: They bought a **dilapidated** old barn and spent three years making it into a home.
Nobody has lived in that **dilapidated** cottage for years.
items.watchOut: Dilapidated кажуть про будівлі й речі в дуже поганому стані, не про людей. Близькі слова: run-down (занедбаний), derelict (покинутий і напівзруйнований). Наголос на другий склад: diLApidated.

items.pattern: a draughty hall / room / house / window · a draught (US draft, drafty) · adjective + noun
items.meaning: with cold air coming in through gaps around doors or windows
items.example: We put a curtain over the front door because the **draughty hall** was freezing.
more: Our bedroom is so **draughty** that the curtains move when the window is shut.
We put a long cushion along the bottom of the door to stop the **draught**.
items.watchOut: «Протяг» — a draught, «тут протяг» — it's draughty, а не windy (windy — вітряно надворі). Gh тут читається як f, як у laugh: draught /drɑːft/. Hall у британському домі — передпокій біля вхідних дверей.

items.pattern: a chilly corridor / room / evening · feel / get chilly · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a corridor that is unpleasantly cold
items.example: The **chilly corridor** between the kitchen and the bathroom is the coldest place in the house.
more: It gets **chilly** in the evenings, so bring a jumper.
The waiting room was so **chilly** that I kept my coat on.
items.watchOut: Chilly — неприємно прохолодно, але ще не мороз. Не плутай з chilled (охолоджений: chilled drinks) і chilli (гострий перець): chilly і chilli звучать однаково.

items.pattern: a cramped room / flat / office / kitchen · cramped conditions · adjective + noun
items.meaning: too small for the people or things in it
items.example: Our first flat had one **cramped room** where we cooked, ate and slept.
more: The flat's lovely, but the kitchen is a bit **cramped** for two cooks.
We lived in **cramped conditions** until my parents could afford a bigger house.
items.watchOut: «Тісна кімната» — зазвичай a cramped room (розмовне — a poky room). Tight частіше кажуть про одяг, взуття, гроші й час, хоча it's a bit tight in here теж можливо. Не плутай з crumpled — пом'ятий (про папір, одяг).

items.pattern: a place / home / room of your own · have / get a place of your own · noun + of + my / your / his… + own
items.meaning: a home that belongs to you or that you don't share with anyone
items.example: After three years of sharing with friends, I'm ready for **a place of my own**.
more: When you have **a place of your own**, you can paint the walls any colour you like.
She was forty before she had **a room of her own**.
items.watchOut: «Своє житло» — a place of my own або my own place. An own place так не кажуть: own іде після присвійного слова (my, his, their). Не забудь of: a room of her own, a car of his own.

items.pattern: affordable housing / homes / rents · a shortage of affordable housing · adjective + noun
items.meaning: homes that people on normal or low incomes can pay for
items.example: The town desperately needs more **affordable housing** for young families.
more: Many seaside towns have lost their **affordable housing** to holiday lets.
Students say **affordable housing** is the hardest thing to find in this city.
items.watchOut: «Доступне житло» — affordable housing (те, що можна дозволити собі за ціною), а не accessible: accessible — зручне для людей на візку або до якого легко дістатися. Housing незлічуване: не housings.

items.pattern: take out a (big / 25-year) mortgage · pay off a mortgage · verb + particle + noun
items.meaning: borrow money from a bank to buy a home, and pay it back over many years
items.example: They **took out a mortgage** to buy their first flat and will be paying it back for twenty-five years.
more: We'll **pay off the mortgage** just before we retire.
The bank wouldn't let me **take out a mortgage** until I'd saved a bigger deposit.
items.watchOut: «Взяти іпотеку» — take out a mortgage (або get a mortgage), не take a credit. Позика в банку — a loan, а credit — це «кредит» загалом (buy on credit). Вимова /ˈmɔːɡɪdʒ/: t не читається.

items.pattern: a house-warming (party) · have / throw a house-warming · invite sb to a house-warming party · noun + noun
items.meaning: a party you have when you move into a new home
items.example: We're having a **house-warming party** on Saturday. Bring a friend if you like.
more: My colleagues gave us a plant as a **house-warming** present.
She invited the whole street to her **house-warming**.
items.watchOut: «Запросити на новосілля» — invite sb to a house-warming (party): прийменник to, не on. Пишуть і housewarming разом. Homecoming — це повернення додому, а не новосілля.

items.pattern: leave home (at 18 / to go to university) · no article · verb + noun
items.meaning: stop living with your parents and start living on your own
items.uk: піти з батьківського дому, почати жити окремо
items.example: I **left home** at nineteen and moved to a city where I knew nobody.
more: **Leaving home** was hard, but it taught me to cook and pay bills.
Mum cried for a week when my little brother **left home**.
items.watchOut: Leave home без артикля часто означає «почати жити окремо від батьків»: I left home at 18. Те саме може значити й «вийти з дому» вранці (I left home at 8) — що саме, видно з контексту. Не leave the home: з артиклем звучить так, ніби йдеться про якийсь заклад.

items.pattern: feel / be / get homesick (for sth) · homesickness · verb + adjective
items.meaning: feel sad because you are far away from your home and family
items.example: I loved my new job in Madrid, but I **felt homesick** every Sunday evening.
more: Our exchange student **got homesick** around Christmas, so we cooked her a dish from home.
Living abroad is exciting, but everyone **feels homesick** sometimes.
items.watchOut: Homesick — не «хворий удома» і не homeless (безхатній). Не плутай miss (сумувати за кимось) і be bored (нудьгувати, коли нема чого робити): I'm homesick або I miss home, але не I'm bored of home.

items.pattern: welcome sb home / back · verb + object + home
items.meaning: greet someone warmly when they come back after a long time away
items.uk: радо зустріти когось, хто повернувся додому
items.example: The dog was waiting at the door to **welcome** us **home** after our holiday.
more: We baked a cake to **welcome** Grandad **home** from hospital.
Crowds lined the streets to **welcome** the team **home** after the final.
items.watchOut: Welcome sb home — home без прийменника: не welcome him at home і не to home. Можна й welcome sb back. А welcome to — коли людина приходить кудись уперше: Welcome to our house!

items.pattern: make yourself at home (to a guest) · make yourselves at home (to several guests) · make sb feel at home
items.meaning: said to a guest: relax and act as if this were your own home
items.uk: будь як удома, почувайся як удома
items.example: Here's the spare key. **Make yourself at home** while we're away.
more: Grab a cup of tea and **make yourselves at home**. The others will be here soon.
The hosts told us to **make ourselves at home**, so we put our feet up.
items.watchOut: «Почувайся як удома» — make yourself at home. Feel yourself at home — калька, так не кажуть. Кільком гостям — make yourselves at home.

items.pattern: feel at home (in a place / with sb) · make sb feel at home · verb + at home
items.meaning: feel relaxed and comfortable in a place or with people, as if you belonged there
items.example: Our new neighbours were so friendly that we **felt at home** straight away.
more: Grandma's kitchen is the place where I've always **felt** most **at home**.
The teacher does everything she can to **make** new pupils **feel at home**.
items.watchOut: «Почуватися як удома» — feel at home, без yourself: не I feel myself at home. It feels like home — «це місце як дім», але про себе кажуть I feel at home, а не I feel like home.

items.pattern: a second home (in the country / by the sea) · also a holiday home · adjective + noun
items.meaning: a house or flat you own as well as your main home and use for weekends and holidays
items.example: My aunt has a **second home** in the mountains and spends every August there.
more: They sold their **second home** to help their son buy a flat.
Owning a **second home** sounds lovely, but someone has to cut the grass while you're away.
items.watchOut: «Дача» — найчастіше a second home, a holiday home або a cottage in the country. Summer house у британській англійській — переважно садовий будиночок-альтанка, а country house — великий старовинний маєток.

warmup.explain: Гостю кажуть make yourself at home. Feel yourself at home — калька з «почувайся».

warmup.uk: Ми взяли іпотеку на двадцять років.
warmup.explain: Взяти іпотеку — take out a mortgage (або get a mortgage).

warmup.uk: Ми запросили всіх сусідів на новосілля.
warmup.q: We invited all the neighbours to our ___.
warmup.explain: Новосілля — a house-warming (party). Homecoming — повернення додому.

warmup.q: The living room windows ___ the river.
warmup.explain: Виходити вікнами на щось — overlook sth, без прийменника.

warmup.uk: Першого місяця в Англії я дуже сумувала за домом.
warmup.q: In my first month in England I was really ___.
warmup.explain: Сумувати за домом — be / feel homesick. Homeless — безхатній.

warmup.uk: У нашому передпокої завжди гуляє протяг.
warmup.explain: Протяг у приміщенні — draughty. Windy — вітряно надворі.

warmup.uk: Минулого місяця ми переїхали в нову квартиру.
warmup.q: We ___ our new flat last month.
warmup.explain: Переїхати в квартиру — move into a flat; без додатка — просто move in.

A.q: The ad offers ___ accommodation, from one week to six months.
A.explain: Житло на короткий термін — short-let (або short-term) accommodation. Short-lived — недовговічний.

A.q: Jo lives alone in a tiny ___ flat: one room, plus a shower room.
A.explain: Квартира-студія — a studio flat. Study — кабінет, cabinet — шафка.

A.q: Is the flat still ___ to rent, or has someone taken it?
A.explain: Про житло, яке можна винайняти, — available to rent. Accessible — до якого легко дістатися.

B.q: The council wants to knock down the ___ old blocks of flats, which are falling to pieces.
B.explain: Dilapidated — напівзруйнований, занедбаний. Refurbished — навпаки, оновлений.

B.q: They're ___ up the café over the winter, so it'll look new when it reopens in spring.
B.explain: Do up — відремонтувати, оновити. Make up — вигадати; put up — повісити, поставити.

B.q: My aunt writes her novels in a tiny ___ at the top of the house.
B.explain: Кабінет удома — a study. Cabinet — шафка або уряд.

C.q: Our guests arrived tired after the long drive, so we told them to ___ themselves at home.
C.explain: Make yourself (themselves) at home — будь(те) як удома. Feel yourself at home — калька.

C.q: When did you first ___ home? — At eighteen, when I went to university.
C.explain: Піти з батьківського дому, почати жити окремо — leave home, без артикля.

C.q: It's strange, but I feel more ___ home in my grandparents' village than in my own town.
C.explain: Feel at home — почуватися як удома. Без yourself і без like.

example.title: A place of our own
example.uk:
Минулої весни ми з Томом нарешті виїхали з тісної квартири-студії й переїхали в дім своєї мрії — старий триповерховий будинок у тихому житловому районі. Щоб його купити, ми взяли іпотеку, яку виплачуватимемо ще багато років.

Будинок був доволі занедбаний, а в передпокої гуляв протяг і стояв страшенний холод, тож ціле літо ми його ремонтували. Тепер із просторої вітальні видно річку, а вікна мого затишного кабінету виходять на сад.

У вересні ми святкували новосілля. Кожному гостеві ми казали: «Будь як удома!» — і вже опівночі ми й самі нарешті почувалися тут як удома.
example.en:
Last spring Tom and I finally [[moved out of|b13]] our [[cramped|b17]] [[studio flat|a2]] and [[moved into|a3]] our [[dream home|b1]]: an old [[three-storey|b2]] house in a quiet [[residential area|a7]]. To buy it, we [[took out a mortgage|b20]] that we'll be paying off for years.

The house was rather [[dilapidated|b14]], and the [[draughty hall|b15]] was freezing, so we spent the whole summer [[doing it up|b12]]. Now the [[spacious living room|b3]] [[has a view of|b4]] the river, and my [[cosy study|b5]] [[overlooks|b7]] the garden.

In September we had a [[house-warming party|b21]]. We told every guest to [[make themselves at home|c4]], and by midnight we finally [[felt at home|c5]] there too.
